what.text: This page follows people displaced inside Sudan, as counted by IDMC and by UNHCR, shown side by side and never added together.
At the end of 2025, IDMC estimated 9116896 people living in internal displacement because of conflict and violence, while UNHCR counted 9139309 internally displaced people it protects or assists.
Many others crossed a border: the largest numbers of refugees from Sudan live in Chad and South Sudan.

why.text: Fighting broke out in April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF).
UCDP records armed conflict over the government of Sudan from 2020 to 2025, with the RSF, SLM/A, SPLM/A-North and SFA among the government's opponents.
Earlier, armed groups in Darfur, including JEM and SLM/A, fought the government from 2003, a conflict UCDP records at war level.

when.text: IDMC's figures show internal displacement rising from 4900000 in 2009 to a peak of 11559970 in 2024.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2023 to 2025, after the war between the army and the RSF began.
South Sudan became independent on 9 July 2011, so figures for Sudan before and after 2011 cover different territory.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took inside Sudan or where they are now living.
IDMC also counts new displacements, which count each forced move rather than each person, so someone displaced twice is counted twice.
UNHCR and IDMC give the same figure in 2023 and 2024; this page shows both side by side and never adds them.
